html: Blood pressure is the push of blood against the walls of your arteries. When it stays too high, the heart and blood vessels are under constant strain, which raises the chances of heart disease, stroke and kidney problems.

image.alt: Illustration of a heart with a pulse line
image.caption: High blood pressure usually causes no symptoms, so checking is the only way to know.
image.title: Illustration of a heart with a pulse line

html: A reading has two numbers, such as 118/76. Your care team will tell you what range is healthy for you and how often to check, at the clinic or at home.

• Cook with less salt and fewer packaged foods
  • Get active on most days
  • Keep alcohol low and don't use tobacco
  • Take blood pressure medicine every day as prescribed, even when you feel well
A very high reading comes with chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, changes in vision or trouble speaking.
